title: -te hobe and question words
focus: Obligation with -te hobe (amake jete hobe); questions with ki, keno, kothay, kokhon, ke, kemon, koto.
body:
# -te hobe and question words

**"Have to"**: take the **-te form** of the verb and add **hobe**. You already know the -te form from *khete chai*. The person who has to do it takes **-ke**: **amake** (me), **tomake** (you), **oke** (him/her). Never use *ami* here.

**Questions**: put the question word **where the answer would go**, usually just before the verb. Don't move it to the front like in English.

| Pattern | Romanization | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| amake + -te + hobe | amake jete hobe | I have to go |
| tomake + -te + hobe | tomake khete hobe | you have to eat |
| oke + -te + hobe | oke ashte hobe | he/she has to come |
| ki | tumi ki chao? | what do you want? |
| keno | keno? | why? |
| kothay | kothay? | where? |
| kokhon | kokhon? | when? |
| ke / kake | o ke? / kake? | who? / who (as object, e.g. "who has to")? |
| kemon | kemon? | how? / what's it like? |
| koto | koto? | how much? |

**Examples**

- amake cha kinte hobe: I have to buy tea
- amake ekhon bari jete hobe: I have to go home now
- amake kothay jete hobe?: where do I have to go?
- tomake kokhon jete hobe?: when do you have to go?
- amake ki korte hobe?: what do I have to do?
- amake koto dite hobe?: how much do I have to give?
- kake jete hobe?: who has to go?
- tumi kothay thako?: where do you live?
- tumi keno jete chao?: why do you want to go?
- khabar-ta kemon?: how's the food?
- cha-ta koto?: how much is the tea?
- beral-ta kothay?: where's the cat?

Other -te forms to use with hobe: korte (do), dite (give), nite (take), kinte (buy), bolte (say), dekhte (see), thakte (stay).

**Common mistakes**

- ❌ *ami jete hobe* → ✅ **amake** jete hobe. With hobe it's always amake / tomake / oke.
- ❌ *ki tumi chao?* for "what do you want?" → ✅ tumi **ki** chao? The question word goes right before the verb.

cards.Notes: amake (me) + khete (to eat) + hobe (will be) = 'it will be for me to eat'
tomake (you) + jete (to go) + hobe; always tomake, never tumi, with hobe
oke (him/her) + ashte (-te form of asha, to come) + hobe
amake + cha (tea) + kinte (-te form of kena, to buy) + hobe; the object goes before the verb
aste aste (slowly) + bolte (to speak) + hobe

cards.English: I have to go home now
cards.Notes: ekhon (now) + bari (home) + jete hobe; with 'go', bari needs no ending

cards.English: Where do I have to go?
cards.Notes: kothay (where) goes right before the verb, not at the front

cards.English: When do you have to go?
cards.Notes: kokhon (when) goes right before jete hobe

cards.English: Why do I have to eat now?
cards.Notes: keno (why) goes just before the verb phrase

cards.English: What do I have to do?
cards.Notes: ki (what) + korte (-te form of kora, to do) + hobe

cards.English: How much do I have to give?
cards.Notes: New: koto = how much / how many; dite = -te form of deoa (to give)
New: kake = who + -ke, like amake/tomake; hobe needs kake, not ke
tumi + kothay (where) + thako (you live/stay)
Lit. 'you what want?'; ki sits where the answer would go

cards.English: Why do you want to go?
cards.Notes: keno (why) + jete chao (want to go)
kokhon (when) + khao (you eat, habitual present)
Lit. 'he/she who?'; no word for 'is' needed
khabar-ta (the food) + kemon (how / what's it like); no 'is' needed
cha-ta (the tea) + koto (how much); handy for asking prices at a shop
beral-ta (the cat) + kothay (where); no 'is' needed
